parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation exists; gender identity discrimination has been criminal since 2005 and the equality statute reaches goods, services, health and employment. No dossier entry documents any traveler-facing exposure: border/document handling, facilities, detention placement and police conduct toward trans visitors are unresolved rather than adverse. Documented negatives are societal: rising recorded hate-crime suspicions (SOGI ~12%), LGBT-wide bullying and a 2018 assault uptick — but motive sits outside the criminal code, counts lack denominators, and the state shows functioning institutions plus reform momentum (conversion-practice prosecution, ban endorsed). Minor-relevant care is centralised and therapy-first, affecting residents more than visitors. This sits in Low Risk, modestly below jurisdictions documenting traveler-specific enforcement of protections.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. Entry, visa, passport-marker and screening rules are unsourced and unresolved.
entry_documents.protection: Outbound 2025 travel advice for the country's own trans citizens shows state alignment with trans travellers, but it is not destination-side protection.
entry_documents.interaction: How a foreign passport with marker mismatch would be handled at the border is an open question, not a documented exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented. No arrest, detention or custody-placement record for trans people appears.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented protocol; institutions are generally functioning, which supports recourse in principle.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Unresolved how an outed visitor would be placed or treated in custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. Gendered-facility access is unsourced; no bathroom or facility restriction appears.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Equality statute covers goods and services since 2014, a paper protection not shown operating for visitors.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Unresolved whether service providers would accept foreign documents; no documented refusals.

care_services.exposure: Over 40% of trans respondents unable to access needed care (undated survey); minors' care centralised with therapy-first 2020 recommendations — largely resident-facing.
care_services.protection: Health services covered by equality statute; blockers remain available case by case.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor seeking local care could face restricted pathway; not documented for visitors.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Rising recorded SOGI hate-crime suspicions (72→241 over six years; 12% of 1,808 in latest year); no hate-crime offence in code, motive recorded only as suspicion.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: First conversion-practice prosecution convicted; parliament endorsed a statutory ban 125–49.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Police record motive despite no hate-crime statute — institutional engagement, not hostility.

minors_guardians.exposure: 2019 findings: LGBT youth face more bullying, violence including at home — LGBT-wide, not trans-specific, resident-sphere.
minors_guardians.protection: Case-by-case blocker availability; guardianship and marriage/adoption framework inclusive.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor faces everyday-sphere friction risk at most; no traveler-facing rule documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 73 violent anti-LGBT attacks in 2018 (+27%), rising SOGI category; no trans-specific killing rate in record.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police count and record motive; discrimination criminal since 2005; strong civil-society infrastructure since 1974.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: No denominator, so magnitude uncertain; no documented pattern of police failing trans victims.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Open questions: border handling, facility access, custody placement, currency of the 2020 care recommendations, final conversion-ban status.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Equality and discrimination statutes in force; conversion practices prosecutable as assault.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unanswered questions are not exposures; no documented adverse outcome for a visitor anywhere in the record.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vessalia documents explicit gender-identity equality law, functioning oversight and only isolated officer friction — closely similar. This dossier has comparable criminalised discrimination and strong protections but slightly more documented societal hostility (rising SOGI hate reports, LGBT youth victimisation) and no traveler-tested enforcement record, sitting just below.

Alderland documents actual nightlife assaults plus partial police failure. This dossier shows no documented trans-specific attack on a visitor, a functioning prosecution route (conversion-practice conviction), and a legislature moving toward further protection — it sits above that anchor.

Kestrel Isles has a documented, recurring border screening exposure for trans visitors. This dossier documents no such exposure; its negatives are societal counts without denominators and unresolved border questions — clearly above, since an open question is not an operative constraint.

Vellmaris shows a documented traveler actually stopped and held, softened by working courts and remedies. This dossier documents no visitor-specific adverse incident at all, plus stronger statutory coverage, placing it above 0.65.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is protective on paper and demonstrably moving further: criminalised gender-identity discrimination since 2005, equality statute extended in 2014, a conversion-practice conviction secured by prosecution, and a ban endorsed by parliament. No traveller-facing restriction, arrest, facility exclusion, custody placement or documented visitor incident appears anywhere in the record; the unresolved axes (border documents, facilities, custody) are open questions, which weigh lightly. Documented negatives are societal-sphere: rising but denominator-less hate-crime suspicion counts, LGBT-wide youth victimisation, and undated care-access gaps. Functional institutions and state alignment with trans travellers keep those signals from compounding. The rating sits in Low Risk, held slightly below the top anchors because documented hostility exists and no visitor-facing remedy has been shown operating.
